case_name: Arjunan v State Represented By Inspector of Police and others
respondent: State Represented By Inspector of Police
facts: The Order of the Court was as follows: ...

The five appellants before us (A-3 to A-7) along with others were tried in Sessions Case No. 20 of 1994 by the Additional Sessions Judge, Thiruvalluvar and by judgment and order dated 12-4-1996 they were sentenced to various terms of imprisonment.
We may notice that the appellants, who were Accused 5, 6 and 7 before the trial court, were charged of the offences under Sections 148, 307/149, 364 and 302 IPC.
The question arises as to whether the conviction of these appellants under Section 148 IPC is justified.
In order to convict the appellants of the offence under Section 148 IPC, it was necessary for the High Court to first record a finding that they were members of an unlawful assembly.
So far as Accused 3 and 4 are concerned, who are appellants in the appeal arising out of SLP (Cri.) No. 2677 of 2005, they were released on bail pursuant to an order dated 13-5-2005.
So far as the remaining appellants are concerned, they were found guilty only under Section 148 IPC and they were also released on bail pursuant to the order dated 15-10-2004.
issues: whether the conviction of these appellants under Section 148 IPC is justified
court_reasoning: In order to convict the appellants of the offence under Section 148 IPC, it was necessary for the High Court to first record a finding that they were members of an unlawful assembly.

Therefore, we are satisfied, in the facts and circumstances of the case, that there was neither any finding nor any material on record on the basis of which the appellants could have been convicted of the offence punishable under Section 148 IPC.
holding: Their conviction and sentence under Section 148 IPC is therefore set aside and they are acquitted of the charge.
All the appeals are allowed accordingly.
cases_cited: Arjunan v State Represented By Inspector of Police
